title: AgriManager: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM-RL Generalization in Agricultural Management
claim: A unified interface wraps heterogeneous simulators so numeric states and actions become text an LLM policy can act on and be trained on via RL.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, arrows looping through central vertical interface bar
description: A wide three-zone diagram. On the left, a grey panel holds a cartoon of corn plants growing in soil with 'water' and 'nutrition' labels. Below it, three rows pair crop models (DSSAT, WOFOST, Cycles) with their gym wrappers (gym-DSSAT, WOFOST-Gym, Cycles-Gym) through double-headed arrows. In the center, a tall vertical bar labeled 'Unified Env Interface' sits between orange boxes. Numerical State [3.52, 0.255 ...] flows right and becomes Textual State: s, a natural-language sentence. Textual Action: a (a Think/Answer response) flows back and becomes Numerical Action [2.0]. A Numerical Reward box reads 'yield - cost'. On the right, a grey panel holds an 'AI' brain icon labeled Agricultural Decision Model. An upward 'Policy Update' arrow runs from stacked s, a, r rollout cards. Peach and orange boxes with bold black arrows.
caption: The AgriManager framework architecture. The "Agri-Gyms" layer wraps the three crop simulators; the environment adapters and Unified Env Interface translate the numerical state-action representation into the text consumed by the LLM decision model; rollouts $(s, a, r)$ drive policy updates.
abstract: Agricultural management is heterogeneous along two axes. The first is distributional shift within a fixed task interface: weather, crops, and prices vary across years and locations while sensors, actions, and objective stay fixed. The second is structural shift across interfaces: different farms expose different observed variables, available actions, and management objectives. We formalize the second axis as schema shift: variation in the policy-facing schema $Î£= (Î£_O, Î£_A, Î£_R)$ between training and deployment. We test whether LLM-RL generalizes across both axes with AgriManager, to our knowledge the first framework that trains LLM policies with RL across multiple process-based crop simulators, unifying DSSAT, WOFOST, and Cycles. We design a three-tier generalization ladder: Tier 1 within-schema distributional shift, Tier 2 single-axis schema shift along $Î£_O / Î£_A / Î£_R$, Tier 3 compositional schema shift across simulators, all scored on a frozen held-out test suite with three training seeds per method. Within fixed schemas, Qwen3-4B trained by RL with explicit reasoning exceeds neural-network PPO trained with the same interaction budget; without reasoning, training stalls near no-action where the reward penalizes input use. Under single-axis schema shift, $Î£_O$ transfer needs decision-critical state, $Î£_A$ results are consistent with joint action-menu coverage, and with reasoning a policy trained on yield alone transfers to unseen objectives. Under compositional schema shift, single-source training mostly hurts zero-shot transfer across simulators, and a unified policy trained only on other combinations of the same components recovers about 86% of the gain of a specialist trained on the target combination on DSSAT and stays below the specialists on the WOFOST and Cycles profit targets. Project page: https://agrimanager-framework.github.io
